chunks: Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub from al-Abbas from Ibn al-Mughira from Ghiyath from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) from his father (peace be upon him) who said:
He said: 'A woman is a row, two women are a row, and three women are a row.'
ai.seo_question: How many women make up one row in congregational prayer according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the jurisprudential definition of a 'row' (saff) for women in congregational prayer, establishing that up to three women form a single complete row. This ruling is significant in Shia fiqh for determining the validity of the congregation when the number of female worshippers is small, distinguishing it from the male arrangement where multiple rows are typically required even for few individuals. It reflects the practical application of prayer geometry in the early Shia community as recorded by Shaykh al-Tusi.
